feedbacks: This is incorrect. VaR is NOT always coherent, especially with fat tails.

questions.question: A bank uses Monte Carlo simulation to estimate VaR. After 10,000 simulations, the portfolio value is less than $90 million in 500 cases. The initial portfolio value is $100 million. What is the estimated 95% VaR?
feedbacks: Correct.  VaR = Initial Value - Value at the α-level where α is (100% - Confidence Level). Here, α is 5% with 5% of 10,000 simulations = 500 simulations. VaR = $100M-$90M = $5M.
questions.explanation: The 95% VaR is the loss that is not exceeded in 95% of the simulations. In this case, the 5th percentile loss is $10 million, so the VaR is $100M - $90M = $10M.

questions.explanation: Backtesting involves comparing the frequency of VaR exceedances to the expected frequency based on the confidence level.

questions.question: A bank uses Monte Carlo simulation to estimate VaR. After 10,000 simulations, the portfolio value is less than $90 million in 500 cases. The initial portfolio value is $100 million. What is the estimated 95% VaR?
feedbacks: Correct.  VaR = Initial Value - Value at the α-level where α is (100% - Confidence Level). Here, α is 5% with 5% of 10,000 simulations = 500 simulations. VaR = $100M-$90M = $5M.
questions.explanation: The 95% VaR is the loss that is not exceeded in 95% of the simulations. In this case, the 5th percentile loss is $10 million, so the VaR is $100M - $90M = $10M.
